working_title: Recent rainfall predicts week-long richness elevation and species-selective reassembly in active frog communities
central_claims: Within fixed route × seasonal-window strata, active-community richness is higher at day 0, day 1, days 2–3, and days 4–7 since reported rain than at >=8 days since rain.
The prespecified run-level richness-pulse endpoint is days 4–7: +0.381 species relative to >=8-day runs, 95% CI 0.202–0.561.
A stricter exact-consecutive-year dry-anchor sensitivity clearly supports positive richness differences through days 2–3 and is directionally positive but imprecise at days 4–7.
Within matched route × seasonal-window comparisons, greater rainfall contrast predicts higher active-species richness.
Rainfall-associated richness gain is not simple nested addition; exact consecutive-year comparisons show increased compositional turnover with rainfall contrast.
Species wet-versus-dry responses remain strongly heterogeneous after pair-level environmental and temporal adjustment and remain heterogeneous within major families.
interpretation: Recent rainfall is associated with a multi-day expansion of the acoustically active frog community and species-selective wet–dry reassembly. The response is not confined to the immediate day of rain.

timescale_boundary.supported: Active-community richness elevation remains detectable through the prespecified 4–7 day recency bin in the route-season fixed-effects analysis.
timescale_boundary.strict_sensitivity: Exact-consecutive dry-anchor richness differences are clearly positive through days 2–3 and imprecise at days 4–7.
timescale_boundary.not_supported: Persistence of compositional turnover above dry–dry temporal background is not established because the prespecified dry–dry minimum sample-size gate failed before effect readback.
timescale_boundary.no_half_life: No physiological recovery time, half-life, or exact decay breakpoint is authorized.

mechanistic_followups.pooled_body_size: strong pooled correlate but family-stratified permutation null; not mechanism authority
mechanistic_followups.hydroperiod_flags: nonestimable because all 23 covered species were coded for both temporary and permanent breeding waters
mechanistic_followups.baseline_episodicity: unsupported in temporal holdout; baseline recurrence P=0.698 and seasonal concentration P=0.990
mechanistic_followups.route_dryness_context: unsupported in temporal holdout; richness interaction P=0.855, exact-consecutive P=0.334
mechanistic_followups.compositional_memory_vs_dry_dry: not estimable; no candidate background rule reached the frozen >=100 pairs and >=50 routes threshold

prohibited: rainfall causes a week-long community state
rainfall causes occupancy or abundance change
compositional turnover is proven to persist for a week
the 4–7 day bin is a physiological recovery time or exact half-life
temporary-water breeding, breeding-season breadth, baseline rarity, or historical route dryness explains species selectivity
body size is a proven mechanism
the ecological-extension analyses were original preregistered hypotheses
